policy_title: Provide free education for military personnel
stated: Reform UK will provide free education for military personnel both during and after service, which they deem vital for a successful return to civilian life.

source.quote: Education for Military Personnel Free education both during and after service is vital to ensure a successful return to civilian life.

bearing_set.reason: Directly funds and expands education access for a defined population (military personnel), affecting skills acquisition and opportunity both in-service and during transition to civilian life.
Post-service education support materially affects servicemembers' employability, pay prospects, and quality of work on return to civilian employment.

Free education for all military personnel (during and after service) is a new or materially expanded spending commitment with no stated funding mechanism, plausibly widening the deficit — a concrete O12 harm via the unfunded-spending pathway.

membership_note: Policy has three clear bearings: a direct education-access improvement (O7), a labour-market-transition improvement (O4), and a plausible unfunded-expenditure cost (O12). Effects on aggregate prosperity (O13) or inequality (O14) via this relatively small beneficiary group would be negligible at population scale.
